newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Dutch stocks to retrace from recent highs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Dutch stocks to retrace from recent highs.

text.p: Shares on the Amsterdam stock exchange are forecast to drop by the end of this year as lower-than-expected corporate earnings from 1996 are released, a Reuters survey showed.

The mean of forecasts from eight analysts to the Reuters international equity index survey, carried out last week, showed expectations of a fall of 6.5 percent on the Amsterdam Exchange Index to 711.9 by end-1997 from 758 on March 13.
But the new consensus is higher than the mean 643.4 forecast from the previous quarterly survey carried out in December.
By end-1998 the index will have recovered to rise by 6.2 percent to 808.3 from current levels, the survey showed.
PETER WORTEL, HEAD OF RESEARCH, DELTA LLOYD BANK:

"I suppose if there is a correction we would expect fundamentally to be finishing 1997 at around 700, 710, not much higher than that. Our reasoning is based on interest rates, the overall profit growth of stocks."
"Just based on profit growth and interest rates we wouldn't have grown in 1996 as we did."
KEES DE VAAN, EQUITIES STRATEGIST AT MEESPEIRSON:

"At the moment the market is more than fully valued if you take into account earnings growth, which is rather high, and bond yields. We expect earnings to grow around 20 percent this year and around 11 percent next year. We see the 10-year bond yield to be 6.1 percent at the end of this year. We are about 10 to 12 percent overvalued according to our models."
